exact_variant: Official English Chatterbox-Turbo model, checkpoint repository ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo; named checkpoint file t3_turbo_v1.safetensors. Official sources identify Turbo as a 350M-parameter streamlined architecture with a distilled one-step speech-token-to-mel decoder. No sub-variant/version beyond these names is specified in the cited model materials.
parameter_count: 350M parameters (official GitHub README and model card).
reported_weight_size: Hugging Face checkpoint page reports t3_turbo_v1.safetensors as 1.92 GB (rounded page display; exact bytes not published/found). Hugging Face API reports 4,046,204,143 bytes of total repository storage, which includes repository artifacts and is not a weights-only measurement. Total weights-only bytes: not published/found.
text_description_voice_design: Not demonstrated as natural-language speaker-description-only voice design. The official Turbo example generates with audio_prompt_path set to a reference clip; no documented prompt such as ‘make a warm, low-pitched older voice’ substitutes for that clip. Paralinguistic tokens can direct reactions/performance, but that is not evidence of designing a speaker identity from text alone.
reference_audio_cloning: Yes—zero-shot voice cloning from reference audio, explicitly documented by the official model card and repository. Turbo’s example passes audio_prompt_path (example filename indicates a 10-second clip); Resemble’s product page claims a few seconds/about 5 seconds suffice. This is reference-audio cloning, not text-only custom voice design.
language_and_control_coverage: Turbo is listed as English-only. Documented native paralinguistic tags include [cough], [laugh], [chuckle]; Resemble’s product page also shows [sigh], [gasp], [whisper], [breath]. Tags express vocal reactions/performance. Resemble describes emotion control, but the cited Turbo usage materials do not provide a sufficiently specific named Turbo emotion/style parameter interface; natural-language speaker-description control is not documented. Do not generalize the family’s 23-language coverage to Turbo (that coverage is for multilingual variants).
code_license: MIT. GitHub repository metadata identifies MIT, and the official LICENSE file is MIT with the standard copyright/permission notice and warranty disclaimer.
weights_license: MIT according to the official Hugging Face Turbo repository’s license metadata (license:mit / cardData license: mit); Resemble’s official Turbo page also states the model is MIT licensed. This is distinct evidence from the GitHub code LICENSE. Check the linked license terms before redistribution/use.
cpu_memory_and_runtime_evidence: The official materials advertise Turbo as lower-compute/lower-VRAM than earlier Chatterbox and claim up to 6× real-time on a single GPU / roughly 75 ms latency on GPU, but publish no RAM minimum, GPU model/VRAM minimum, or CPU benchmark for Turbo. The README’s Turbo loading example uses device="cuda"; the separate 110M Nano variant is the one explicitly said to run on CPU (3× realtime on 8 cores), which must not be attributed to Turbo. Therefore CPU-only performance/feasibility for this machine’s 8 cores and 23 GiB RAM is not established by cited sources; no specific required RAM can be claimed. Documentation says tested on Python 3.11 / Debian 11; compatibility with the user’s Python 3.12.3/Linux setup is not established there. No install or download was performed.
quality_ranking_evidence: No comparable public rank found specifically for Chatterbox Turbo. Artificial Analysis’ live human-vote Elo leaderboard shows an entry named only ‘Chatterbox’ (listed as May 2025, Elo 1021, position 70 in the returned table), not Turbo; it is unsafe to transfer that score/rank to this variant. Separate Podonos Turbo head-to-head pages expose pairwise overall score summaries: Turbo vs ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5: 0.69 shown with ElevenLabs as Model B and 1,052 Turbo-favoring answers (42.08%); vs Cartesia Sonic 3: 0.17 shown with Cartesia as Model B and 766 Turbo-favoring answers (30.64%); vs VibeVoice 7B: 0.50 shown with VibeVoice as Model B and 999 Turbo-favoring answers (39.96%). These are pairwise evaluation results, not a cross-model rank; reports do not show an evaluation date in the fetched pages. Podonos’ overview describes the reports as human-perception comparisons. Access/retrieval date: 2026-10-10; not the benchmark date.
github_popularity_evidence: GitHub API repository metadata returned 26,444 stars and 3,560 forks on 2026-10-10 (retrieval date). These are popularity proxies only, not quality evidence or a model-specific Turbo count.
integration_notes: Local Python package is documented as pip install chatterbox-tts, with source install also documented; Python usage exposes ChatterboxTurboTTS.from_pretrained(...) and generate(..., audio_prompt_path=...). The repository’s Turbo sample uses CUDA. Official materials also offer a hosted Resemble AI playground/service, but the cited local documentation does not establish a Turbo local HTTP/REST API or guarantee CPU support. User should treat Python 3.12.3 and CPU-only inference as unverified compatibility/runtime questions, rather than assume installation and inference will work within the available hardware.
caveats: Audit status date is 2026-10-10. No package or model was installed/downloaded.
A marketing claim of high quality or head-to-head competitiveness is not a ranked benchmark; Podonos result pages omit the benchmark date in the content fetched.
The Artificial Analysis ‘Chatterbox’ leaderboard row does not identify Turbo, so its Elo/rank is not attributed to Turbo.
Turbo’s advertised performance is GPU-focused; the CPU performance claim in the official README concerns Chatterbox-Nano, not Turbo.
The main checkpoint is shown as rounded 1.92 GB; exact checkpoint bytes and total weights-only bytes were not published/found in the opened source pages.
Python 3.11/Debian 11 is the documented tested environment; Python 3.12.3 support and a RAM/CPU minimum are not published/found.
Natural-language speaker-description-only voice design is not documented for Turbo; do not conflate audio-reference cloning with text-only voice creation.
